reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the high mobility of Mn and its role in forming layered, porous oxides in CrFeCoNiMn, but provides no data on Al or Si additions, nor any comparison of cation diffusion rates between Al, Mn, and Si variants. The key premises about Al reducing diffusion and Si behaving like Mn are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mn in CrFeCoNiMn leads to layered Mn-rich outer oxides and Cr-rich inner oxides due to outward cation diffusion
Mn has high mobility and low-energy oxide formation, causing pore formation and accelerated oxide growth
Al addition reduces outward diffusion of metal cations in CrFeCoNiX alloys
Reduced cation diffusion promotes a continuous, Cr/Al-rich protective oxide layer that is thinner and more adherent
Mn or Si addition leads to faster cation diffusion and thicker, non-uniform scales prone to cracking
